issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds vol of every M-column submatrix of a false instance by induction from k=2. The base case treats only pairs of sets sharing one or two elements and concludes vol(hat-mc_2) = 2*sqrt(2)/3 for 'matrices with k=2 columns'. Two distinct sets of a false X3C instance can be disjoint (falsity of X3C only guarantees that SOME pair in every M-collection intersects, by the pigeonhole argument quoted from Theorem t_volptas); for a disjoint pair the two columns are orthogonal and vol = 1 > 2*sqrt(2)/3. Hence the base statement is false, the induction proves nothing for submatrices containing disjoint pairs, and the gap bound needed for the theorem (vol <= 2*sqrt(2)/3 for EVERY M-column submatrix) is not established.

We derive an inapproximability threshold of $(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only transfers the volume gap: on true instances sopt = 1, on false instances sopt <= (2*sqrt(2)/3)^{1/k}. This gap is instance-dependent and tends to 1 as k grows, while the reduction yields instances of arbitrarily large k. For any fixed epsilon > 0 there are false instances with k large enough that the optimum exceeds 1-epsilon, so a hypothetical (1-epsilon)-approximation algorithm is not excluded on them. Refuting a PTAS requires a gap bounded away from 1 by a constant; the k-dependent gap established here does not give one, so the sentence 'Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS' does not follow from the argument.

Since all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)\leq 1$, (\ref{e_ortho}) can only 
hold if all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)=1$.
Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to~1, and $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

\rvol(\mc) \equiv\frac{\vol(\mc)}{\|\mc\|_2^k}=
\prod_{j=1}^k{\frac{\sigma_j(\mc)}{\sigma_1(\mc)}}

issues.failure_explanation: From the product of factors sigma_j/sigma_1 equal to 1 the proof correctly infers that all factors equal 1, i.e. that all singular values are EQUAL (to sigma_1); it then asserts they equal 1, so that the columns are orthonormal. This is false: any matrix with mutually orthogonal columns of common norm s > 0 has rvol = 1 (e.g. mc = 2*[e1 e2] has vol = 4, ||mc||_2 = 2, rvol = 1) without being orthonormal. The correct equivalence is with orthogonality of the columns, not orthonormality.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'orthonormal' by 'orthogonal' in the lemma's equality characterization (all singular values equal, i.e. mc^T mc = sigma_1^2 I), and in Theorem thm:rvolnp add the one-line observation that the reduced instance has unit-norm columns, so an orthogonal submatrix is orthonormal.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:orth's 'only if' direction is false, and the proof of Theorem thm:rvolnp, which invokes the equivalence 'orthonormal iff rvol = 1', is unsound as written (it survives once the unit-norm column assumption of the reduced instance is used). The upper bound rvol <= 1 and its use in Theorem t_volptas are unaffected.
issues.title: Relative-volume equality case: rvol = 1 also for non-orthonormal orthogonal columns
issues.why_classification: A one-word correction plus a trivial observation (columns of the reduced instances are unit norm) restores every use of the lemma, including the reduction in Theorem thm:rvolnp; no substantive claim is lost.

Applying the pinching inequality~\cite[Equation (IV.52)]{Bhatia97} gives

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's central step equates the Schatten-(p/2) norm of a block-diagonal matrix with the sum of the norms of its blocks. This additivity holds only for the trace norm (q = 1, i.e. p = 2, the Frobenius case handled in Lemma l_fi); for q = p/2 > 1 the Schatten-q norm of a direct sum is (||A||_q^q + ||B||_q^q)^{1/q}, strictly less than ||A||_q + ||B||_q. The stated inequality is in fact false: with mc = I_2 split into its two columns (rank(mc) = n = 2) and p = 4, the left side is ||I_2||_{(4)}^2 = sqrt(2) while the right side is 1 + 1 = 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma with p-th powers, ||mc^dagger||_{(p)}^p >= ||mc1^dagger||_{(p)}^p + ||mc2^dagger||_{(p)}^p for p >= 2; the same pinching argument proves it because ||diag(A,B)||_{(q)}^q = ||A||_{(q)}^q + ||B||_{(q)}^q for q = p/2 >= 1.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma l_pi1's stated inequality is false; no later labelled result invokes the lemma, so no dependent result is invalidated.
issues.title: Partitioned Schatten p-norm lower bound is false as stated
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality must be weakened (squares replaced by p-th powers), a contained nontrivial correction that preserves a comparable partitioned-norm bound; the lemma is unused elsewhere, so no further loss occurs.
